Every entry names the documents it applies to, the model, the target piece list, the seat where the book or the slip states one, the desc2Match that tells one build on a document from another, and a why recording how the answer was reached. Four entries are the owner's own reading, given in chat; the rest are read off the photograph and confirmed by him. 2026-09-08: HC-SO-013475 was added to this same file rather than a new one - a fourth file whose name also contains "2026-09" would make the FILE= substring filter select two rounds at once (scripts/lib/sofa-corrections-source.test.mjs pins that), and this build carries its own why, which is where the evidence has to live. It is NOT a placeholder build: it is the shop floor reporting that the drawing and our decode disagree. 2026-09-08 ROUND 2: 16 more builds, all of them the owner's OWN words given in chat while he read his slips one by one. They are appended to THIS file rather than a new one for the reason the previous sentence gives - a fourth file whose name also contains "2026-09" would make the FILE= substring filter select two rounds at once, which scripts/lib/sofa-corrections-source.test.mjs pins. Two of them (HC-SO-012827) are matched on the account book's own LINE KEY rather than on text, because the book wrote one line's Desc2 as a substring of the other's and no needle can tell them apart. 2026-09-08 ROUND 3: the TWO builds round 2 deliberately held are now written, and `_held` is EMPTY. Each was held for a real reason and each reason is gone, because he gave the missing word himself. HC-SO-011601 had only its corner and its seat; the rest of the slip was read off the 240px original enlarged 4x, put to him, and confirmed 「对啊」. HC-SO-011657 was held because 9838-STOOL is not minted and nobody held the judgement of which model a `TNS-9838 DB` stool belongs to; he answered 「那就放8030 daybed把」. An answered build may not sit in `_held`: the operator's log prints held builds as outstanding work and makeSofaRulingLookup excludes them, so parking an answer there keeps handing him back a question he has already settled (docs/bugs/0720). HC-SO-011657 is also the first entry to carry `modelOverride` - the ERP names a product the book does not, by his decision, and the declaration is what lets the grader tell that from the hand-typed model of docs/bugs/0693. 2026-09-08 (second round, same day): the owner re-read the enlarged slips of HC-SO-011733, HC-SO-012025 and HC-SO-013384 and gave six answers. TWO of them - HC-SO-012025's first sofa and HC-SO-013384's first sofa - CONFIRM entries already in this file, and that confirmation is recorded in their own `why` rather than duplicated as new entries. HC-SO-012025's second sofa is written as an entry below. HC-SO-011733's re-reading and HC-SO-013384's second and third sofas are in `_held`, each carrying the measured reason it is not written - and for HC-SO-011733 that reason is a question only he can close, not a limitation of the tooling. Still no fourth file: a name also containing "2026-09" would make the FILE= substring filter select two rounds at once, which scripts/lib/sofa-corrections-source.test.mjs pins. 2026-09-09: the 1ELT entry now names the WHOLE CHAIN of its sofa - the sales order, the purchase order, the goods receipt, the delivery order and the sales invoice - because the owner answered all four documents with the same build and because a build written on one side leaves the others holding the lead piece alone (docs/bugs/0719). A document that is not a sales order or a purchase order is a DOWNSTREAM document: the applier does not raise it, it brings it to the build's own shape by adding the pieces it has no row for, and it refuses anything that is not migrated paperwork. The SECOND sofa the book's GR-000287 carries is in _held: his answer is written down in full and the ERP holds no row to put it on - the five other documents of that sofa's chain are not in the ERP at all. Still no fourth file whose name contains "2026-09", for the reason this note has already given twice.
_rules: Money never moves: the price rides the FIRST piece and every other piece is 0. Lines are matched to target pieces and UPDATED in place so a row id - and any purchase allocation hanging off it - survives. A document can hold MORE THAN ONE sofa build, so desc2Match is required; where a document holds TWO lines with the SAME text those are two identical sofas and both take the build. Where a document holds two sofas that NO needle can tell apart - because one build's text is a strict SUFFIX of the other's - the second build carries a `desc2Exclude` as well: the rows carrying that text, byte-exactly, are not this build. An exclusion that matches no row on the document is a REFUSAL, never a quiet widening back onto both sofas.
